verdict.rationale: Lium documents programmatic start (`lium up`, `POST /executors/rent-by-spec`) and termination (agents remove pods, TTL and spend-cap auto-deletion), with per-second billing and no minimum. The evidence never shows stopping, pausing, or restarting a pod, so only half of the lifecycle verbs are covered. Missing for 10: documented stop/pause and restart of instances, billing behavior for stopped instances, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can start, stop, restart, and terminate instances programmatically and keep paying only for what is running

citations.quote: rent-by-spec (`POST /executors/rent-by-spec`) that rents the cheapest node matching a GPU spec under a `max_price_per_gpu_hour` ceiling
An agent can do everything on Lium with no browser: sign up, fund, rent, connect and remove pods.
You pay **per second**: `hourly price × seconds / 3600`, with no minimum.
Pick one, and the pod is deleted when it is reached: Hours... End time... Spend cap: a budget in USD
